recipes.name: Red Lentil Curry
ingredients_raw: 3 cups water, or more as needed

steps.text: Wash lentils in cold water until water runs clear.

Put lentils in a pot with enough water to cover; bring to a boil and reduce heat to medium-low. Cover and simmer, adding water as needed to keep lentils covered, until tender, 15 to 20 minutes. Drain.
Heat vegetable oil in a large skillet over medium heat; cook and stir onions in hot oil until caramelized, about 20 minutes.
Mix together curry paste, curry powder, turmeric, cumin, chili powder, salt, sugar, garlic, and ginger in a large bowl; stir into onions.
Increase heat to high and cook, stirring constantly, until fragrant, 1 to 2 minutes.
Stir in tomato puree and lentils; cook until warmed through.

raw_recipe.headline: Red Lentil Curry
raw_recipe.description: This red lentil curry is a rich and hearty vegetarian curry made with caramelized onions, spices, and tomato puree for a filling and satisfying meal.

review.reviewBody:
Very tasty. This recipe will vary in taste and heat according to your curry paste. 

Notes about lentils: I have never cooked lentils before so I thought I would share some tips for others like me. 

First off, they are very small so don't try to use a strainer with larger holes (Yes, I know this is obvious). Rinse them well until the water runs clear.
 
Wet lentils stick to everything! Try to get them in the right pot the first time. I found a spatula was good for transferring them. 

Red lentils cook fast! I boiled mine for 2 mins then simmered for about 8 mins. At that point they were mostly tender. I transferred them into the sauce, mixed well and let them finish cooking. They didn't get too mushy like many people have mentioned.

I have never sent a review for any recipe that I have tried. But, this recipe deserves one! It is excellent. I used fresh tomatoes and then put them into the caramelized onions. I also simmered all the spices together in a little oil, as taught to me by an Indian cook. Then, tossed in the garlic and ginger; continued for about 1 more minute. Afterwards, I put the tomato and onions into the spice mix. Then, added the lentils... AWESOME!

I can't believe I never reviewed this recipe. I've been making it once a week for a long time now - it's excellent. The ONLY thing I changed with the recipe was to replace the tomato puree with one can of Muir Glen Fire Roasted Chopped Tomatoes. It gives it a much better texture and the fire roasted tomatoes just add another level of flavor that regular tomatoes don't.

I can't believe how many people are making this without curry paste. It's the most important ingredient in a curry. 

I serve it with jasmine rice and hot naan. Oh, and don't be alarmed if the lentils look rather mushy before you add them to the spices and tomatoes. You haven't done anything wrong, and they'll still taste just as good. :)

Yum! Will make again. Boiled lentils for 2 minutes then simmered with lid for another 8 minutes, stirring occasionally. 
As suggested by another, I used fire-roasted tomatoes in place of puree. I doubled ginger and garlic. I omitted chili powder by mistake, but didn't miss it and found it to have just enough spice anyway. Added 1/2 cup chicken broth at the same time as the tomatoes for a looser consistency. Served over rice that had been made with chicken broth and lemon zest and sprinkled with chopped cilantro. May add steamed green peas to serve next time.

I just made this and it is very delicious. However, I made a little change to it: I used half the tomato paste and added vegetable broth to cook the lentils and the onion and spices mix, on low heat for about 15 minutes so everything became well blended together.

I'm not too experienced with curries, and when I opened the jar of red curry paste I purchased, I was very disappointed. It tasted like tomato paste with tumeric. Just awful. So I didn't add the tomato puree. Instead I added finely diced poblanos, zuchini, and mushrooms, and a good dose of my own curry powder and cayenne. I didn't drain the lentils because I didn't want it too thick. Served over rice, it was delicious!

COMFORT FOOD. Although I am of European heritage, I have eaten curry all my life (thanks, Mom) and this dish is fabulous. Used Madras curry paste; had about 2 T of paste so used 1.5 cups of blended diced tomato. I think the liquid really added to the dish. Did everything else as listed. I do like spicy but this was enough. Added a cup of frozen peas. Nutrition, lower cost meal--can't beat it!

I used my Instapot to cook the lentils (two minutes on high pressure). The Instapot can also be used to sauté the onions and spices before adding the lentils and cooking. I added in the tomato purée after I cooked everything. It was incredibly quick and easy, and very tasty!

This was an easy and delicious recipe. I didn’t have Indian curry paste so I used Thai red curry paste but only 1/2 T. because it’s spicy. I also had some roma tomatoes that needed to be used so I added those chopped up. It turned out great and tastes good with cucumber raita and chapati.

This was sooo good! I didn't intend to make any changes but...I did not have curry paste but did have a 15oz jar of Patak's curry simmer sauce. So I omitted the tomato puree and just used the Patak's curry sauce and it was delish. This is a keeper. Will definitely be making again.
read notes, cook spices in oil first. Used more canned/diced tomatoes. Feel free to add some coconut milk/cream as well. Delish!

I overcooked the split lentils, and I didn't have any fresh ginger. I also added a can of coconut milk without realizing it wasn't called out in the recipe. It was still most excellent! I've always used coconut milk in my curries and will continue to do so. This was fabulous! My husband doesn't do spicy, so I use yellow curry paste, but I have dried scotch bonnet and added that to my bowl. Thanks so much for a fabulous curry recipe!

I have stage 4 kidney disease from chemo rather than diabetes, so I have been looking for low salt recipes that aren't bland and to cut red meat for plant protein. This was my first time using lentils and this recipe is easy and adaptable (the comments about reducing cooking time helped). I can control the salt and plan to switch up spices depending on what dominant taste I'm in the mood for: curry, Italian, Mexican, spicy or mild, garlic, onion, peppers. Leftovers are great. I'm adding this as a regular, inexpensive, healthy meal.
Delicious and a nice change from the usual meat and sides dinner. I did cut the red curry paste by 1/2, since the brand I use is extremely hot.

Kind of gross. My lentils were mushy, way over cooked and the flavor was kind of bitter or off in some way. I don't think turning the heat up high when mixing the spices was advisable. Would not make this again. This curry was way better: https://www.allrecipes.com/recipe/212721/indian-chicken-curry-murgh-kari/

We both liked this recipe. I did have some changes, out of necessity: 1. substituted hot gochujang paste for red curry paste, used 1/2 the amount called for in the recipe 2. added 1 cup of roast turkey chunks (had to use them up!) 3. added a half-cup of water to the mixture after stirring in the cooked lentils 4. added 10 fresh cherry tomatoes, halved, to the mixture last just before serving
